title: Reimbursement and Billing Manual, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program: Billing Units on a Renewal Authorization Grant
content:
## Section R-1. Billing units carried by a renewal grant

Under the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, the authorization grant that Larkfield Medical Supply writes from a renewal written order for the CGM supply allowance (HCPCS A4239) on the CGM Original Medicare Program carries a whole number of billing units fixed by this section. One billing unit of the CGM supply allowance is one 30-day supply of sensors.

**R-1.1 Formal clause: the grant.** The grant carries the order's billing units per 30 days times the whole 30-day blocks from the order date through the order's valid-through date, both days counted, and is anchored to the order date; the order is the newest written order of the item on the program.

**R-1.2 Formal clause: the coverage review.** When the customer has stopped insulin, that is when the customer's insulin pharmacy program is closed with closure reason "customer discontinued", and the CGM program documents an insulin regimen (multiple daily injections, an insulin pump or basal insulin only), the grant's counted blocks, the blocks of its span, never exceed the months left of a coverage review, blocks added on top of the span not counting toward that limit: the review length is the 30-day blocks of one standard shipment, in months; the review starts on the later of the review visit, the latest visit on the program's medical records with purpose continued-need follow-up or initial qualification by any practitioner, and the regimen change date, the ship date of the latest insulin refill on the customer's insulin pharmacy program, either date counting as earlier than every record when no such record exists; and the months left are the review length less the whole calendar months from the review start to the grant's anchor date, counted as zero when the review start falls after the anchor date, and never below zero.

**R-1.3 Records of the item.** The grant still valid on the order date is the authorization grant of the item with the latest valid-through date when that date is on or after the order date; the latest refill is the latest refill shipment of the item, read for its ship date and supply days, and with no refill on record its ship date counts as the order date and its supply days as 0. Whole calendar months from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day.

**R-1.4 Order of settlement.** Each adjustment of the grant changes it as that adjustment states, in this order: replacements of a standard quantity are applied first, so the span's blocks and the anchor date are those as replaced; the coverage-review limit is then applied to the span's blocks so replaced, counting the months left to the anchor date so replaced; blocks added on top of the span come last and are not limited by the coverage review; the blocks are settled before they are multiplied by the units per 30 days, and the grant then carries a whole number of units.

| Term | Reading on the customer's records |
|---|---|
| The order | the written order of the CGM supply allowance on the program with the latest order date, read for its order date, its valid-through date and its quantity per 30 days |
| Units per 30 days | the order's billing units per 30 days, the quantity per 30 days stated on the order |
| The span's blocks | the whole 30-day blocks from the order date through the order's valid-through date, both days counted; a remainder of fewer than 30 days adds no block |
| The anchor date | the order date |
| Stopped insulin | the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is closed with closure reason "customer discontinued" |
| Insulin regimen documented | the CGM program records multiple daily injections, an insulin pump or basal insulin only as the customer's insulin regimen |
| Review length | the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment divided by 30, in whole blocks, read as that many months |
| Review visit | the latest visit date among the clinical documents on the CGM program's medical records whose purpose is continued-need follow-up or initial qualification, whoever the practitioner |
| Regimen change date | the ship date of the latest insulin refill shipment on the customer's Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program |

**When the review limit bears on the grant.**

| Insulin pharmacy program closed with closure reason "customer discontinued" | Insulin regimen documented on the CGM program | Counted blocks |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the fewer of the span's blocks and the months left of the coverage review |
| yes | no | the span's blocks |
| no (open, or closed for any other reason) | any | the span's blocks |

Read clause by clause, the review start is the later of the review visit and the regimen change date; with only one of them on record it is that one; with neither on record it counts as earlier than every record, so the whole calendar months to the anchor date exceed any review length and no month of the review is left. A review start after the anchor date counts as zero months, leaving the whole review length.

## Section R-2. Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

**R-2.1 The span.** Suppose, purely for illustration, an order dated 1 March of a hypothetical Year 1 with a valid-through date of 8 June of Year 1, stating 7 billing units per 30 days, on a customer whose insulin pharmacy program is open. The span runs 100 days, both ends counted, which holds 3 whole blocks with 10 days left over that add nothing. The grant carries 7 times 3, that is 21 billing units, anchored to 1 March of Year 1.

| Days of the span, both ends counted | Whole 30-day blocks |
|---|---|
| 89 | 2 |
| 90 | 3 |
| 119 | 3 |
| 120 | 4 |

**R-2.2 The coverage review.** Take a hypothetical anchor date of 10 April of Year 1, a customer who has stopped insulin with multiple daily injections documented, and suppose the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment were 150 days, giving a review length of 5 months.

| Review start | Whole calendar months to the anchor date | Months left of a 5-month review |
|---|---|---|
| 20 January of Year 1 | 3 calendar months, less one because the 10th is earlier than the 20th: 2 | 3 |
| 10 January of Year 1 | 3 | 2 |
| 20 January of Year 0 | 15 calendar months, less one: 14 | 0 (never below zero) |
| 15 May of Year 1 (after the anchor date) | counted as zero | 5 |

With a review visit of 20 January of Year 1, a latest insulin refill shipped on 5 December of Year 0, a span of 9 blocks and 7 billing units per 30 days, the review starts on 20 January of Year 1, the months left are 3, the counted blocks are the fewer of 9 and 3, that is 3, and the grant carries 7 times 3, that is 21 billing units. Every figure in this section is a hypothetical input chosen to show the counting and is not a program value.
